findings.reason: the real defect is that the newly-introduced refusal (a-live-worker-can-be-reached §9) trips on the suite's documented no-answer stub, so the repair belongs in how "no answer" is distinguished from "answered and untrusted"; a node briefed on the spawn story would either chase codex availability, weaken the stub instead of exercising the no-answer path, or relax the production refusal that §9 requires, and none of those makes the 12 tests pass while keeping a live launch trusted.
findings.text: §70's Why states the 12 dispatching tests fail because "building a codex worker's argv … starts a real codex app-server" so "a test that dispatches with a codex backend therefore spawns codex", and that they fail "on a compute node, where codex cannot start"; measured at head e8c403db, `tests/test_a_source_file_is_shared_by_default.py::test_two_dispatches_share_a_file_under_a_declared_root` fails in 9.3 s with **zero** `codex` execve attempts under strace -f (the autouse `no_live_account_probe` at tests/conftest.py:490-503 replaces `_backends.run_probe` with `lambda probe: None`, so `_inbox_hook_flags` raises without ever spawning), while the same test with `RECKON_TEST_DISABLE_ACCOUNT_PROBE_GUARD=1` makes 9 `codex app-server -c hooks.PostToolUse=…` execve attempts and still fails after 28 s on this login node where codex is on PATH; the guard has been in place since dceecd3028 (2026-10-03), five weeks before fc6561cb69
